newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates stabilise after pact.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates stabilise after pact.

text.p: Dutch call money rates stabilised at a slightly higher level on Thursday after the Dutch central bank allocated fresh liquidity to the money market under a four day advances pact.
The central bank allocated 2.88 billion guilders at an unchanged advances rate of 2.50 percent.
Call money, very volatile in recent days swinging from 2.00 to 2.81 percent bid - was trading at around 2.62 percent in the middle of the afternoon.
Dealers said they did not foresee big movements in overnight money rates in the near term.
The weakening of the guilder against the mark had no disturbing effect on the market, dealers said. The Dutch currency was trading at 112.19 per 100 marks from 112.13 yesterday.

"An exchange rate up to 112.20 per 100 marks is not unpleasant for the market," said one dealer, adding a weakening towards 112.40 would not be all that worrying. "But above that it is time to deal with it," he said.
Most deposits were trading just a fraction higher. Three-month deposits were bid at 2.72 from 2.70 on Wednesday.
